feat(export): shared export resolution for HTML and SVG (rich-export-9a1.1) (#150)

* feat(export): resolve recorded output into the rows both exporters draw (rich-export-9a1.1)

The research ticket asked for design/export-pipeline.md. CLAUDE.md forbids a
second description of a subsystem outside docs/, so the design lands as the
module that makes it true, with the rationale in its header and the claims
pinned by tests.

src/core/export-lines.ts resolves a recorded Segment stream under a
TerminalTheme into rows of { text, look } runs. ExportLook carries only
resolved values: reverse, dim, conceal, default colours and the theme's ANSI
table are consumed here, so neither the HTML nor the SVG exporter can forget
one. parseHref is the single checkpoint for links an export may publish
(http, https, mailto, ftp, file); a refused link keeps its text.

Nothing consumes it yet: rich-export-9a1.2 routes exportHtml through it and
deletes the two style-to-CSS converters it replaces.

* fix(export): flatten alpha before reverse, dim and conceal (rich-export-9a1.1)

resolveLook handed translucent colours straight to the swap, the fade and
conceal. toSgrCodes flattens first, so an exported #rrggbbaa run drew other
colours than the terminal did, and conceal over a translucent background left
the glyph visible. Paper now flattens over the theme canvas and ink over the
paper, through ColorSpec.flattenAlpha, before anything else sees them.
